title: Dave Grohl - Wikipedia
notes: Read to character 200,000 of 242,094. David Eric Grohl, born 14 January 1969, Warren, Ohio; the family moved to Springfield, Virginia; parents divorced when he was seven. Guitar at 12, self-taught; switched to drums when Freak Baby reshuffled into Mission Impossible; no formal lessons, taught himself by listening to Rush and punk; hearing 2112 at eight: 'It made me want to become a drummer'; John Bonham his greatest influence, the three-rings symbol tattooed on his shoulder; the 9:30 Club as the source of early influences. Joined Scream at 17, replacing Kent Stax, lying about his age; No More Censorship, Fumble (wrote and sang Gods Look Down), Your Choice Live Series Vol. 10; drums for Iggy Pop in Toronto, 1987. Buzz Osborne passed his availability to Cobain and Novoselic; first heard on Nevermind (Sound City); the Scentless Apprentice riff ('kind of boneheaded', Cobain). Foo Fighters debut: every instrument but Greg Dulli's guitar on X-Static; drummed for Tom Petty and the Heartbreakers in 1994; re-recorded The Colour and the Shape's drums (Goldsmith: 'Dave had me do 96 takes of one song'); Taylor Hawkins replaced Goldsmith, died March 2022. Songs for the Deaf (2002) and the No One Knows video; Them Crooked Vultures (2009); Probot (2004); Tenacious D (2001, Rize of the Fenix 2012); Killing Joke (2003); six tracks of Nine Inch Nails' With Teeth (2005); Ghost's If You Have Ghost; Rolling Stone's 27th-greatest drummer (2016); Rock and Roll Hall of Fame with Nirvana (2014) and Foo Fighters (2021).

title: Nirvana (band) - Wikipedia
notes: Read to character 100,000 of 222,066. Drummers: Aaron Burckhard (1987, 1988), Dale Crover (the first demos, January 1988; filled in on the August 1990 West Coast tour with Sonic Youth), Dave Foster (1988), Chad Channing (May 1988 to 1990, left as the others grew dissatisfied with his drumming), Dan Peters (the Sliver single, July 1990), Dave Grohl (from September 1990, introduced by Buzz Osborne after Scream broke up). Novoselic: 'We knew in two minutes that he was the right drummer.' Guitar World: his drumming 'took Nirvana's sound to a new level of intensity'; Azerrad: propelled the band 'to a whole new plane'. Reading 1992 headline; In Utero at Pachyderm with Albini, February 1993; MTV Unplugged, November 1993.

title: Nevermind - Wikipedia
notes: Read to character 100,000 of 210,131. DGC, 24 September 1991; produced by Butch Vig and Nirvana; Sound City, Van Nuys, 2-28 May 1991, mixed 1-9 June; demos at Smart Studios, April 1990, with Chad Channing (only Polly carried over, with Channing's cymbal crashes). Grohl: drums, backing vocals (In Bloom, Drain You, On a Plain), co-writer of Smells Like Teen Spirit. Andy Wallace's mix 'most notably altered the drum and guitar'; he used kick and snare samples to drive reverbs rather than replace the drums.

title: In Utero (album) - Wikipedia
notes: Read to character 100,000 of 187,480. DGC, 13 and 21 September 1993; produced by Steve Albini at Pachyderm, Cannon Falls, Minnesota, 13-21 February 1993, mixed by 26 February; basic tracks played live as a band; Very Ape and Tourette's drums recorded in a kitchen for its reverb; about 30 microphones round the kit; Albini: 'If you take a good drummer and put him in front of a drum kit that sounds good acoustically and just record it, you've done your job.' Scentless Apprentice and Gallons of Rubbing Alcohol credited to all three.

title: Live at Reading - Wikipedia
notes: Reading Festival, 30 August 1992, closing night; released 2 November 2009 (Geffen, CD and DVD), filmed by Fujisankei. Grohl: drums, backing vocals; after Territorial Pissings he took the kit apart and threw his cymbals at it. Grohl (Kerrang!, 2018): 'a really reassuring, genuinely magical moment of everything coming together at the right time.'

title: Live at the Paramount (video) - Wikipedia
notes: Paramount Theatre, Seattle, 31 October 1991; about 2,800 people; filmed on 16 mm, 'the only Nirvana show to be shot entirely on 16 mm film'; released 24 September 2011 (DGC) with the Nevermind 20th anniversary. Grohl: drums, backing vocals. Mudhoney and Bikini Kill on the bill.

title: Foo Fighters (album) - Wikipedia
notes: Read to character 100,000 of 114,117. Roswell/Capitol, 26 June 1995 (UK), 4 July (US); produced by Grohl and Barrett Jones; Robert Lang Studios, 17-23 October 1994; every instrument Grohl's but Greg Dulli's guitar on X-Static; about four songs a day, in track order, Grohl 'still sweating and shaking from playing drums' as he picked up the guitar.

title: The Colour and the Shape - Wikipedia
notes: Read to character 100,000 of 133,011. Roswell/Capitol, 20 May 1997; produced by Gil Norton; Bear Creek, Grandmaster and WGNS, November 1996 to February 1997. Grohl re-recorded Monkey Wrench's drums, then most of the album; William Goldsmith's drums remain on Doll and the slow intro of Up in Arms; Goldsmith left; Taylor Hawkins hired as recording finished.

title: Songs for the Deaf - Wikipedia
notes: Read to character 100,000 of 108,092. Interscope, 27 August 2002; produced by Josh Homme, Eric Valentine and Adam Kasper; October 2001 to June 2002 at The Site, Conway and Barefoot. Grohl on drums, replacing Gene Trautmann (drums on tracks 1 and 8); Homme invited him in October 2000; Grohl's last show with the band July 2002, Joey Castillo his replacement. Drums tracked in a small, dead isolation booth for a 'tight, focused, punchy and kind of claustrophobic' sound; each song played twice, first on electronic cymbal pads, then with real cymbals over a dummy snare and padded toms, and the takes blended; Valentine praised his patience.

title: Probot (album) - Wikipedia
notes: Southern Lord, 10 February 2004; recorded 2000-2003 at Studio 606, Alexandria, Virginia, engineered by Adam Kasper. 'Dave Grohl played the majority of instruments on the album, including all of the drum tracks.' Singers from ''82 to '89 underground metal': Cronos, Max Cavalera, Lemmy, Mike Dean, Kurt Brecht, Lee Dorrian, Wino, Tom G. Warrior, Snake, Eric Wagner, King Diamond.

title: Them Crooked Vultures (album) - Wikipedia
notes: Interscope/DGC (US), Columbia (UK), November 2009; recorded January to August 2009 at Pink Duck (Burbank) and Chalice (Hollywood); produced by the band. Grohl: drums, percussion, backing vocals, production.

title: Scream (band) - Wikipedia
notes: Northern Virginia, formed 1981 (Pete and Franz Stahl, Skeeter Thompson, Kent Stax); Stax left after Banging the Drum (1986); Grohl, 'then 17-year-old local drummer', lied about his age to tour with them; No More Censorship (1988, RAS); Live at Van Hall (1988); Your Choice Live Series Vol. 10 (Alzey, spring 1990); Fumble released 1993, three years after the break-up; Grohl rejoined for a 1993 tour.

title: Live Nirvana Equipment Guide: Dave Grohl
notes: Fan archive drawn from tech and photo sources. '90-'91: Tama Granstar in Silky Yellow, Superstar snare in Natural ('demolished at the Cabaret Metro, Chicago, 10/12/91'); then Granstar II in Fire Storm Red with an Artwood snare in Black (photo 27 October 1991) for the rest of the US Nevermind tour; In Utero tour: Artstar II in Piano Black, Superstar snare, and a Rockstar-Pro. Sizes 8x14 birch snare, 14x15 rack tom, 16x18 floor tom, 16x24 bass drum. Zildjian A Medium: 18 and 20 crashes, 22 ride, 15 hi-hats; only As, except a 28-inch Paiste ride/crash with Scream. Heads: Aquarian Hi-Energy snare ('the only brand that wouldn't break'), Remo Pinstripe tom batters over Clear Ambassadors, changed every show; Clear Powerstroke II kick batter, Ebony Ambassador front with a 6-inch off-centre hole. Tama Titan hardware, a Sonor hi-hat stand (the only one tall enough); DW 5000 Turbo pedal, three carried. Regal Tip 5B and Aquarian Power-Sleeve 2B; held upside-down.

title: Stuart Williams, ''We've got a new drummer, his name is Dave, he's the best drummer in the world!': How Dave Grohl delivered the incredible Smells Like Teen Spirit drum track', MusicRadar, 3 July 2026
notes: Cobain's tape to Vig: 'he's the best drummer in the world!'; Vig to Howard Stern (2022) on hearing it in rehearsal; Sound City; Grohl used a Tama Granstar ('not Artstar II, as commonly reported') with gear rented from Drum Doctors, including a Ludwig Black Beauty and a Tama Mastercraft Bell Brass snare; Vig's mics (D12 kick, SM57 snare, 421s on toms, 414 overheads, two U87 room mics 15-18 feet back); Grohl, Classic Albums: 'I didn't throw a bunch of drum fills in there. I tried to keep it as simple as possible', 'like children's songs'; the intro's flams with even sixteenths between them; Grohl to Pharrell (From Cradle to Stage): 'I pulled so much stuff from The Gap Band and Cameo, and Tony Thompson', 'The big disco flam', Thompson: 'I know.'; the chorus's foot-heavy first beat with two crashes; the verse with the snare on 2 and 4, the kick in eighths with the bass, hats closed but for a lift on the 'and' of 4 every fourth bar; the pre-chorus kick pushing; sixteenths on the snare into the chorus with an eighth-note kick under the roll, 'Ringo-style', Grohl 'a huge Beatles fan'; 'heavy-hitting, neanderthal style'.

title: Terry Gross, 'Dave Grohl retraces his life-affirming path from Nirvana to Foo Fighters', Fresh Air, NPR, 31 December 2021 (transcript)
notes: Recorded November 2021 for The Storyteller. One drum lesson, a jazz drummer who told him he held the sticks backwards: 'For loud, brash, dissonant, distorted punk rock, it absolutely works... if I hold it like a hammer... I still do it to this day.' Learned 'on pillows on my bedroom floor' with oversized marching sticks to fast punk records, 'like running in the sand', then 'I would just destroy' a real kit; Scream 'mercilessly pummeling these drum sets'. Nirvana: 'The drumming is very simple', songs in one or two takes; 'if my drumming in the punk rock band was 250 beats per minute, my drumming for Nirvana - I sometimes liken it to, like, disco drumming and funk drumming'; the flam on Come As You Are and Teen Spirit, 'from, like, the Gap Band or Cameo or Power Station'; 'a sign of a great drummer is when their song comes on at a bar and people that don't play the drums air drum along'. 'The Beatles were my first teacher.'

title: Kory Grow, 'Dave Grohl, Reed Mullin Explain Punk Supergroup Teenage Time Killers', Rolling Stone, 28 July 2015
notes: Grohl: 'Reed was my drumming hero when I was 15 or 16 years old'; Animosity 'the Odessey and Oracle of fucking crossover hardcore metal albums', 'I've stolen so many of his fucking riffs'; 'ripping to my favorite drummer [Corrosion of Conformity's] Reed Mullin'. Mullin: in D.C. in the early 1980s (Bad Brains, Void, Scream, Minor Threat) he met 'this one kid' over a shared love of Chuck Biscuits; 'he followed me around and learned how I did triplets and stuff like that. It took him, like, two weeks to figure out all the shit I knew how to do.'

title: Hank Shteamer, 'Reed Mullin, Corrosion of Conformity Drummer, Dead at 53', Rolling Stone, 28 January 2020
notes: Repeats Grohl's 2015 words: Mullin 'my drumming hero when I was 15 or 16 years old', and on Animosity, 'I've stolen so many of his fucking riffs from that record'.

title: Elijah C. Watson, 'How Black Drummers Influenced Nirvana's "Smells Like Teen Spirit"', Okayplayer, 24 September 2021
notes: Collects Grohl's words: From Cradle to Stage (2021), 'I pulled so much stuff from The Gap Band, and Cameo, and Tony Thompson'; Rolling Stone (2001), Teen Spirit 'a dance beat - the verses are like Cameo-disco drumming and the choruses are heavy-metal Sixties go-go'; Spin (February 2013), 'disco drums', 'A lot of the drum fills I did I took from Cameo and the Gap Band'; Bad Brains: A Band in D.C. (2012), 'I still use a lot of the tricks that I learned from Earl still to this day', 'there's little fills here and there that I took from Earl'. That Earl Hudson's fill is the basis of the Teen Spirit intro is the author's reading, not Grohl's.

title: '100 Greatest Drummers of All Time', Rolling Stone, 31 March 2016
notes: Entries 100 to 51 read (Grohl's own, no. 27, not reached). Earl Hudson: 'Nirvana's Dave Grohl admits to swiping his moves for the intro to "Smells Like Teen Spirit" and told Modern Drummer, "I would learn all of [his] licks verbatim."' Dale Crover: Grohl, 'you can tell when Dale is playing in Nirvana because he's the best drummer in the world', 'if things didn't work out [with me], they could always get Dale'. Matt Cameron: Grohl, 'Nobody played drums like Matt.' Jon Theodore: Homme, 'Dave was, like, "You know, the guy who really blows me away is Jon Theodore"'. Jimmy Chamberlin: 'grunge-era Zeppelin-ites like Nirvana's Dave Grohl or Soundgarden's Matt Cameron'.

title: Martin Kielty, 'Dave Grohl Was "Branded for Life" by John Bonham Obsession', Ultimate Classic Rock, 17 January 2021
notes: Quotes a Guardian interview (January 2021, not read directly): 'I had learned to play drums by arranging pillows on my floor and my bed in the formation of a drum set', playing along to Bad Brains; 'I became obsessed with John Bonham: what he played and why'; 'his feel and sound is unmistakable and undefinable'; 'Anyone can take the chart of what he played, but it would never be the same'; 'I gave myself a three-interlocked-circles John Bonham tattoo on my arm with a fucking sewing needle and some ink. I was branded for life.'

title: Drumeo, 'Dave Grohl: Everything You Need To Know About The Nicest Guy In Rock' (updated 1 November 2023)
notes: Nirvana: Tama Granstar 14x15 rack tom, 16x18 floor tom, 16x24 bass drum, 8x14 Superstar birch snare; Zildjian A Custom 18 and 20 crashes, 22 ride, 15 hats (Live Nirvana says A Medium); then a red Granstar II and a black Artstar II. Endorses DW. Them Crooked Vultures: DW Jazz Series 9x13 rack tom, 16x16 and 16x18 floor toms, 16x20 gong drum, 16x24 bass drum, 6.5x14 aluminium snare. 'Hard-hitting beats with fun, inventive fills'; plays 'what's best for the song'.

title: Joe Rosenthal, 'QOTSA Enjoying Life With Dave', Rolling Stone, 3 May 2002
notes: Coachella, April 2002: 'every time Grohl landed one of his pummeling fills'; shirt off halfway. Nick Oliveri: 'He's got a signature beat, and I don't know many drummers that have that, you know, the "Teen Spirit" beat. That's Dave Grohl's beat as far as I'm concerned'; 'a better drummer' than singer or guitarist; 'He's a madman.'

title: Nirvana, Live at the Paramount (16 mm film of 31 October 1991; YouTube GcuFXCKcMac, 'Dave Grohl - Drums - Live at the Paramount', and tGc8jL4dzao, 'Breed (Live At The Paramount/1991)')
